svg.title: Suspected hip fracture worked through the lecture's approach: is it a fracture, is the patient stable, why did they fall and why did the bone break, then surgery within 24 to 48 hours chosen by fracture type (femoral neck non-displaced or displaced, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric), and the after-surgery plan to prevent complications, falls and the next fracture

svg.text: Suspected HIP FRACTURE (= a proximal femur fracture)

svg.text: risk = whatever raises the risk of FALLS + whatever raises the risk of OSTEOPOROSIS

svg.text: high suspicion in an older person even if the pain or the trauma was minimal

svg.text: sudden groin or lateral upper-thigh pain after a fall · worse moving and weight bearing

svg.text: leg SHORTENED, EXTERNALLY ROTATED and ABDUCTED · cannot weight bear · painful log roll and straight leg raise

svg.text: 1 · X-ray: AP (front-to-back) pelvis + hip · negative but suspicion still high → CT

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 2 · STABLE? airway, breathing, circulation (young, high-energy) · pelvic fracture? · check distal pulses + nerves, especially the

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 3 · WHY did they fall? complete blood count (CBC), electrolytes, troponin · ECG (atrial fibrillation?) · chest X-ray (pneumonia?)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 4 · WHY did the bone break? a pathologic fracture (bone tumour)? · a fragility fracture qualifies as OSTEOPOROSIS → start that

Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 5 · Plan: SURGERY within 24–48 hours for the VAST majority

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: quicker return to weight bearing · fewer complications of lying still · the X-ray's fracture type picks the operation ↓
